instruction:
We're handling the equipment installation for this single-story, long-span steel-frame workshop, and next month I need a render for our monthly progress review with the owner and the site supervisor — something that clearly shows the structure and the equipment layout. Please follow the on-site photo exactly for the spatial relationships; don't re-lay-out the space: a large rectangular hall on a steel frame system, one exterior wall lined with tall vertical strip windows, and a green self-leveling epoxy floor. Within that fixed space, place all the main things visible in the shot — the several large stainless processing machines mounted on steel platforms with yellow safety railings, the runs of silver insulated ducts and process pipes above and beside the machines, the green vertical cylindrical tank standing on the floor in front of the platforms, and the blue roller conveyor line across the front area; fill in the connecting bits like stairs and support hangers to typical site practice, with counts, positions and orientations only roughly matching the photo — estimate sizes by proportion and normal industrial specs. The key thing is that the connections between the steel members read clearly and the overall scale and the machine-to-building proportions are right, so we can add callouts on it during the review. Make it a daytime scene, keyed off the daylight through the side windows, for a bright, clean, modern production-hall feel. Put the camera close to the photo viewpoint — slightly high, looking diagonally down the depth from one end of the conveyor toward the machines. Materials, lighting and render settings are all in the attached `scene_spec.yaml`, follow that. Use colors that keep the different components distinguishable. Deliver a 3840×2160 PNG hero image and keep the Blender project with packed textures so we can update the viewpoint and progress each month.
